text:
customer_ana: Hey team — our dedicated pool (cust-acme-west) didn't scale up during a burst this morning. ~20% request error rate (429s) for ~5m, latency spiked. We were on min_replicas=2, traffic jumped to ~40rps. Any quick fixes?
support_ryan: sorry about that — can you share a timestamp and an example request id? Also any recent changes to reserved capacity? :thinking:
customer_ana: timestamps: 2025-11-07T09:12:08Z -> 09:18:30Z. example request id: req_20251107_09_12_4512. No quota changes on our side. We saw 503s turning into 429s as autoscaler lagged.
eng_oncall_lee: Thanks. I'm looking at control-plane events now. Quick checklist: did the warmchain/warmpool get depleted? Any imagepull or node taints? If you can share pod events that'd help.
support_ryan: also noted a deploy-bot message around 09:11 UTC for a config tweak. @deploy-bot can you paste the deploy note?
deploy-bot: automated-deploy: updated customer-acme-west config: max_concurrency -> 32 (2025-11-07T09:11:22Z). No rolling restart.
sre_chris: That config change could reduce headroom if concurrency per replica increased. If min_replicas stayed at 2, throughput per replica needed to jump 2x. Warmpool depletion + higher per-rep concurrency can cause probe pacing to defer scale.
eng_oncall_lee: Can you run and paste output of these (or give us logs):
```
# list pods and readiness events
kubectl -n cust-acme get pods -l customer=acme -o wide
kubectl -n cust-acme describe pod <failing-pod>
# autoscaler metrics (internal)
curl -sS http://internal-metrics/autoscaler?pool=cust-acme-west | jq .scaleEvents | tail -n 20
```
customer_ana: Pasted snippets: pods show 2 ready, 0 pending. Describe showed ImagePullBackOff on one probe-init container at 09:11:40 but recovered by 09:13. Autoscaler events show a series of "scale_suppressed: reason=handshake_in_progress" entries between 09:12:30-09:16:00.
support_ryan: "handshake_in_progress" entries sound like the attach/handshake with the dedicated allocator block. That's consistent with requests queuing while the control-plane waits for warmchain verification.
sre_chris: Also check for rate caps on the attach API — if attach requests are being rate-limited, autoscaler may stagger spinups. Can you share any gateway error logs for 429s on the attach endpoint?
customer_ana: gateway logs:
```
[09:12:31] attach-api 429 rate_limit exceeded tenant=cust-acme-west burst=10 limit=5
[09:12:44] attach-api 200 attach success tenant=cust-acme-west pod=rp-7
[09:13:05] attach-api 429 rate_limit exceeded tenant=cust-acme-west
```
support_ryan: OK that shows attach throttling. Likely sequence: deploy tweak increased concurrency, traffic burst, attach API rate limit hit -> autoscaler handshake suppressed -> warmpool unable to top up fast enough -> frontdoor returns 429s.
eng_oncall_lee: Short-term mitigation options: lower per-rep concurrency (rollback), increase min_replicas, or request a temporary attach-rate bump from infra team. Also we can enable conservative fallback to a lower-capacity model variant (fallback routing) to bypass attach.
support_ryan: For reproducible steps for ops: 1) run attach-api rate metrics for 09:10-09:20 2) confirm warmpool depletion timeline 3) check recent config changes (max_concurrency) 4) if attach ratecap is root cause, escalate to infra for rate increases.
sre_chris: Notes: watch for imagepull blips — if init containers slow, they extend handshake and amplify attach contention. We saw one ImagePullBackOff window earlier.
support_ryan: I'll open a ticket to infra with logs and request a temporary attach-rate bump. tagging eng-runtime for follow-up on warmchain heuristics. @eng_oncall_lee can you take ownership of the follow-up?
eng_oncall_lee: Taking it. I'll correlate attach-rate metrics + autoscaler state machine traces and propose a fix: either softer handshake backoff or burst credits for verified tenants.
customer_ana: thanks — timeline and actions appreciated. Can you confirm whether we should roll back the concurrency change for now?
support_ryan: short answer: yes if you can, rollback to previous concurrency while we get a rate bump. Otherwise increase min_replicas to 4 as a stopgap.
eng_oncall_lee: will draft a runbook entry for this pattern (concurrency changes + attach ratecap -> scale lag). Posting follow-up here once infra responds. :white_check_mark:
